title: audit-exporter: add customer sinks, retention, terraform wiring & upgrade hooks for Private
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Private installer: audit-log-exporter can now route audit records to customer sinks (S3/GCS/Syslog/Elasticsearch) with configurable retention and optional KMS encryption; Terraform module exposes new sink configuration; Helm chart gains retention, rotation, and upgrade hooks to support zero-downtime migrations.
description:
Context and motivation: Private deployments currently persist audit events only to the local cluster logging layer. Customers running in VPC/on-prem require first-class exports to their sinks (S3/GCS/Syslog/ES) and must be able to control retention, encryption and export scheduling for compliance. This PR wires the audit-log-exporter Helm chart into the private-installer Terraform module, surfaces sink configuration to customers, and adds upgrade/rollback-safe hooks so migrating retention policies does not cause data loss.

Summary of changes: 
- Helm (audit-log-exporter chart): add 'sinks' values (type: s3|gcs|syslog|elasticsearch), per-sink config blocks, retentionDays, rotateCronSchedule, kmsKeyRef optional. Added pre-upgrade/post-rollback hooks to drain and re-initialize exporters. 
- Terraform: private-installer module gains audit_export configuration block with example for s3 and syslog; templates render values.yaml for Helm and preserve secret handling via customer-managed KMS integration. 
- Installer hooks: pre-upgrade job that drains exporter buffers to ensure no event loss, post-upgrade migration that reconciles retention policy and prunes expired records (configurable dry-run). 
- Docs and examples: quickstart snippet for configuring S3/GCS sinks, recommended retention defaults for regulated customers, migration notes. 
- Tests: unit Helm template tests, integration e2e that runs against kind cluster with a fake S3 sink and verifies records arrive and retention pruning triggers.

Checklist: 
- [x] Helm chart changes with unit tests
- [x] Terraform module updates and examples
- [x] Installer upgrade/rollback hooks implemented
- [x] Basic e2e test for sink delivery and retention pruning
- [x] Docs updated (private deployment guide)
- [x] Security review for secret handling and KMS usage

Commits (high-level): 
- feat(helm): add sinks and retention config for audit-log-exporter
- feat(terraform): expose audit_export block and render values.yaml
- feat(installer): add pre-upgrade drain and post-upgrade retention migration jobs
- test(e2e): fake-s3 sink integration test + retention verification
- docs: private deployment audit export quickstart and migration notes

Files changed (high-level): 
- helm/charts/audit-log-exporter/values.schema.json (added sink schema)
- helm/charts/audit-log-exporter/templates/deployment.yaml (env/config injection)
- helm/charts/audit-log-exporter/templates/hooks/pre-upgrade-drain.yaml
- helm/charts/audit-log-exporter/templates/hooks/post-rollback-reinit.yaml
- infra/terraform/modules/private-installer/main.tf (render values.yaml + secret handling)
- infra/terraform/modules/private-installer/outputs.tf (new outputs)
- installer/hooks/drain-script.sh (portable drain helper)
- tests/e2e/audit-exporter/fake-s3-test.sh
- docs/private/audit-exporter.md

CI notes: initial CI run showed lint warnings for terraform fmt and a failing e2e due to timing in the retention prune job (race on fake-s3 object visibility). I pushed a follow-up commit that increased polling time and added idempotent checks; final CI is green (unit + lint + e2e).

Review summary: 
- Nora asked to make KMS usage optional and explicitly document who manages the key (customer vs Redwood). Implemented by adding kms.keySource = ["customer","redwood"] and documenting customer-managed as recommended for regulated customers.
- Liam requested that retentionDays default to 365 for orgs with regulatory needs and not to bake aggressive pruning by default; changed default to 365 and added a 'dryRun' flag for first migration.
- Diego pointed out potential RBAC gaps for the pre-upgrade drain job when run in strict PSP environments; updated the hook Job to use a serviceAccount with minimal aggregated roles and added ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding manifests to the chart with annotation to allow installer to opt in.

Migration notes: When upgrading from versions < 1.2.0 the pre-upgrade hook will run to drain exporter buffers; if customers have retained objects older than the new retentionDays, post-upgrade migration will only mark for deletion (dry-run) unless 'enforcePrune: true' is set. We recommend running in dry-run first and validating output.

Security: Secrets are stored as Kubernetes secrets by default. For Private we render KMS-encrypted secrets if customers supply a kmsKeyRef; Terraform wiring leaves the secret creation to the customer or uses a helper module that can integrate with cloud-provider secret stores. All exported sinks support TLS and credentials stored in secrets.

Why this is safe to merge: Changes are behind Helm values (opt-in) and Terraform defaults keep behavior backward compatible. Hooks are idempotent and include timeouts to avoid blocking install. E2E validates delivery and pruning behavior.

Follow-ups: 
- Add GCS lifecycle rule templates for customers who prefer cloud-side retention instead of in-cluster pruning (ENG-2204).
- Add Prometheus metrics and alerts for exporter queue depth and prune job duration (SRE-ops).
